question: What does it mean when a disease is described as 'endemic' in a community?

options.A: It only affects travellers visiting from foreign countries
options.B: It appears once every ten years and then vanishes
options.C: It is constantly present at a steady baseline level
options.D: It suddenly affects people across multiple continents

explanation: Think of an endemic disease as a constant visitor—it stays within a specific area consistently over time without needing a fresh introduction from outside. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h1)

question: Why is malaria considered an endemic disease in Nigeria?

options.A: Because transmission cycles happen year-round without stopping
options.B: Because it causes sudden outbreaks only during the harmattan season
options.C: Because the federal government eradicated it completely last year
options.D: Because it only affects individuals who travel outside the country

explanation: Malaria remains present at predictable, steady rates in Nigeria throughout the entire year, which is the exact definition of an endemic disease. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h1)

question: What do we call a sudden spike in disease cases that goes way above the normal baseline in a region?
explanation: When an illness suddenly surges and hits way more people than usual in an area, that's an epidemic. Great job keeping these terms straight! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h2)

question: How is a pandemic different from an epidemic?

options.A: It disappears completely after a period of three weeks
options.B: It spreads across multiple countries and continents worldwide
options.C: It only affects livestock rather than human populations
options.D: It maintains a low, steady baseline in a single village

explanation: While an epidemic can be massive, a pandemic goes global, crossing international borders to affect people all over the world. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h2)

question: What are the three core parts of the epidemiological triangle used to study diseases?
explanation: Always remember the trio: the Agent (the germ), the Host (the person), and the Environment (where they meet). Simple and classic nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h3)

question: What role does the environment play in keeping an endemic disease going?

options.A: It builds permanent immunity inside the bloodstream of the host
options.B: It provides external conditions that bring the agent and host together
options.C: It acts as the biological organism that manufactures the toxins
options.D: It develops pharmaceutical treatments to cure the infected population

explanation: Things like warm weather or stagnant water create the right setting for germs and vectors to find human hosts easily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h3)

question: Which animal is well-known as the natural reservoir host for transmitting Lassa fever in West Africa?
explanation: The multimammate rat (Mastomys) carries the Lassa virus and sheds it in homes through its urine and droppings. Good public health detail to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h4)

question: A patient in a rural Nigerian community comes in with a persistent fever in an area where malaria happens all year round. How would you classify this disease pattern?
explanation: Since malaria is constantly present at a steady, predictable level in that community, it is classified as endemic. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h4)

question: Why does a low rate of childhood immunization help keep an endemic disease active in a community?

options.A: It leaves enough susceptible individuals for the infection to keep spreading
options.B: It forces the infectious agent to change into a non-harmful bacteria
options.C: It improves the environmental conditions for vector breeding grounds
options.D: It eliminates the natural reservoir hosts living inside the community

explanation: When fewer children are vaccinated, the germ easily finds new, unprotected bodies to infect, keeping the transmission cycle alive. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a factor that helps sustain an endemic disease in a community?
explanation: Clean water actually stops diseases from spreading! Poor sanitation and lack of clean water are what help infections stick around. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h5)

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance at the primary health care level?

options.A: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.B: To collect taxes from patients seeking medical treatment
options.C: To detect unusual increases in cases early and report them
options.D: To construct new hospital buildings in rural districts

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping a watchful eye on health patterns so health workers can spot a sudden spike before it becomes a major outbreak. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h6)

question: Why is a primary health care nurse in a great position to monitor community diseases?

options.A: They possess the authority to declare national state emergencies
options.B: They interact directly with local patients and see early signs of illness
options.C: They work exclusively inside high-tech research laboratories abroad
options.D: They are responsible for importing vaccines from international suppliers

explanation: Because community nurses talk to patients every single day, they are usually the very first to notice when something unusual is going on. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h6)

question: How do prevention strategies for endemic diseases differ from one-time emergency outbreak responses?

options.A: They focus solely on international travelers rather than local residents
options.B: They are only implemented once every ten years during heavy rainfall
options.C: They require continuous, ongoing community programs rather than temporary fixes
options.D: They rely exclusively on expensive surgical procedures in tertiary centers

explanation: Since endemic diseases are always around, our fight against them through education and vaccines has to be continuous, not just a quick one-time fix. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h7)

question: A community health nurse wants to lower malaria cases in a rural Nigerian village. Which action is the most practical primary health care step?

options.A: Stopping all routine vaccinations until malaria is completely eradicated
options.B: Admitting every healthy villager into the central hospital for observation
options.C: Waiting until an epidemic is declared before taking any action at all
options.D: Distributing insecticide-treated bed nets and teaching mothers how to use them

explanation: Giving out bed nets and showing families how to use them directly protects people from nightly mosquito bites right in their homes. Excellent community nursing in action! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h7)
